body.statement:
Assume \(p\ge 2\) and \(H_0,H_1\succ0\).  The three-snapshot raw fiber \(\mathcal F_3\) is nonempty if and only if
\[
 \lVert H_0^{-1/2}d_0\rVert_2=\lVert H_1^{-1/2}d_1\rVert_2.
\]
When this equality holds, put \(r=\operatorname{rank}(H_0^{-1/2}d_0)\in\{0,1\}\).  Under the bijection
\[
 U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2},
\]
the fiber is noncanonically a torsor for \(O(p-r)\), and its dimension is
\[
 \frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}{2}.
\]
Its intersection with the strict filter set
\[
 \left\{W:\rho(W)<1,\ \operatorname{spec}(W)\cap(-\infty,0]=\varnothing,\ C_0-T_W\succ0\right\}
\]
is relatively open.  Consequently every nonempty local admissible branch or stratum has that same dimension.  If \(d_0\ne0\), then \(r=1\), so three snapshots have continuous local ambiguity for \(p\ge3\).  If \(d_0=0\), nonemptiness is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), the fiber is a torsor for \(O(p)\), and continuous ambiguity occurs already at \(p=2\).  These failures of transition identification transfer to every unknown-common-measurement-covariance model whose model class contains the present stable, embeddable, deterministic Gaussian class as a subclass and has the same transition target.
body.proof_tex:
Because \(H_0\) and \(H_1\) are positive definite by \(\text{ass:strict-decrease}\), their symmetric positive-definite square roots and inverse square roots exist.  Define
\[
 a=H_0^{-1/2}d_0,\qquad c=H_1^{-1/2}d_1,
 \qquad U=H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}.
\]
The inverse change of variables is
\[
 W=H_1^{1/2}UH_0^{-1/2},
\]
so it is a bijection on \(\mathbb R^{p\times p}\).  Direct multiplication gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1
 &\iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0W^{\mathsf T}H_1^{-1/2}=I_p\\
 &\iff UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\\
 &\iff U\in O(p),
 \end{aligned}
\]
where the last equivalence uses that \(U\) is square: \(UU^{\mathsf T}=I_p\) makes \(U\) invertible and hence also gives \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_p\).  Likewise,
\[
 Wd_0=d_1
 \iff H_1^{-1/2}WH_0^{1/2}H_0^{-1/2}d_0=H_1^{-1/2}d_1
 \iff Ua=c.
\]
Thus \(\text{def:three-fiber}\) yields the exact observable representation
\[
 \mathcal F_3\longleftrightarrow\{U\in O(p):Ua=c\}.
\]

If this set is nonempty, orthogonality gives
\[
 \lVert c\rVert_2^2=c^{\mathsf T}c
 =a^{\mathsf T}U^{\mathsf T}Ua
 =a^{\mathsf T}a
 =\lVert a\rVert_2^2,
\]
which proves necessity of the displayed norm equality.  Conversely, suppose \(\lVert a\rVert_2=\lVert c\rVert_2\).  If this common norm is zero, then \(a=c=0\), and every \(U\in O(p)\) is a solution.  If the common norm is positive, extend \(a/\lVert a\rVert_2\) and \(c/\lVert c\rVert_2\) to orthonormal bases of \(\mathbb R^p\).  The orthogonal map sending the first basis to the second sends \(a\) to \(c\).  This proves sufficiency without any unobserved condition.

Fix one solution \(U_0\).  For any other solution \(U\), set \(R_0=U_0^{\mathsf T}U\).  Then
\[
 R_0\in O(p),\qquad R_0a=U_0^{\mathsf T}c=a,
 \qquad U=U_0R_0.
\]
Conversely, every \(R_0\in O(p)\) satisfying \(R_0a=a\) gives the solution \(U_0R_0\), and the representation is unique.  Hence the solution set is a torsor for the stabilizer
\[
 \operatorname{Stab}(a)=\{R_0\in O(p):R_0a=a\}.
\]
If \(a=0\), this stabilizer is \(O(p)\).  If \(a\ne0\), the orthogonal decomposition
\[
 \mathbb R^p=\operatorname{span}(a)\oplus a^\perp
\]
shows that every stabilizer element is the identity on \(\operatorname{span}(a)\) and an arbitrary orthogonal map on \(a^\perp\); hence it is isomorphic to \(O(p-1)\).  Since a nonzero column vector has rank one, these two cases are exactly \(O(p-r)\), where \(r=\operatorname{rank}(a)\in\{0,1\}\).

For completeness, the dimension formula follows locally rather than from a dimension count asserted by name.  At the identity, differentiating \(Q^{\mathsf T}Q=I_s\) gives
\[
 Z^{\mathsf T}+Z=0.
\]
The free entries of a skew-symmetric \(s\times s\) matrix are its \(s(s-1)/2\) entries strictly above the diagonal.  An explicit local chart is the Cayley map
\[
 Z\longmapsto (I_s-Z)(I_s+Z)^{-1}.
\]
For \(Z^{\mathsf T}=-Z\) sufficiently near zero, direct multiplication shows that this matrix is orthogonal.  Conversely, for an orthogonal \(Q\) sufficiently near \(I_s\), the inverse formula
\[
 Z=(I_s-Q)(I_s+Q)^{-1}
\]
is defined and is skew-symmetric.  Thus this is a bijective local coordinate map, and left translation supplies the same chart at every group element.  Taking \(s=p-r\) proves
\[
 \dim\mathcal F_3=\dim O(p-r)=\frac{(p-r)(p-r-1)}2.
\]

We next justify that the dimension is the dimension of the structural, rather than merely algebraic, ambiguity.  Let \(W\in\mathcal F_3\) satisfy the three strict filters in the statement.  Since \(\rho(W)<1\), Jordan normal form gives constants \(A<\infty\) and \(b\in(0,1)\) such that \(\lVert W^j\rVert\le A b^j\) for all sufficiently large \(j\).  Therefore
\[
 T_W=\sum_{j=0}^{\infty}W^jH_0(W^{\mathsf T})^j
\]
converges, is positive definite because its first summand is \(H_0\succ0\), and satisfies
\[
 T_W-WT_WW^{\mathsf T}=H_0.
\]
It is the unique solution: if \(D-WDW^{\mathsf T}=0\), then
\[
 \bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)\operatorname{vec}(D)=0,
\]
and \(\rho(W\otimes W)=\rho(W)^2<1\) makes the coefficient matrix invertible.  Put
\[
 E'=C_0-T_W\succ0,\qquad \mu'_0=m_0,
 \qquad x'= (I_p-W)^{-1}(m_1-Wm_0).
\]
The inverse in the last expression exists because \(\rho(W)<1\) implies \(1\notin\operatorname{spec}(W)\).

The spectral-cut condition gives the real principal logarithm \(G'=h^{-1}\operatorname{Log}(W)\).  Indeed, on a complex Jordan block \(\lambda I+N\), with \(N^s=0\), the principal logarithm is
\[
 \operatorname{Log}(\lambda I+N)
 =\ell(\lambda)I+
 \sum_{q=1}^{s-1}\frac{(-1)^{q+1}}{q}\left(\frac{N}{\lambda}\right)^q,
 \qquad -\pi<\operatorname{Im}\ell(\lambda)<\pi.
\]
The finite nilpotent-series identities show that exponentiating this block returns \(\lambda I+N\).  Conjugate blocks have conjugate logarithms, so the logarithm of the real matrix \(W\) is real.  Since \(h>0\) by \(\text{ass:spacing}\), every eigenvalue \(g'\) of \(G'\) obeys
\[
 \operatorname{Re}(g')=h^{-1}\log|\lambda|<0,
 \qquad -\frac{\pi}{h}<\operatorname{Im}(g')<\frac{\pi}{h},
\]
using \(|\lambda|<1\) from \(\rho(W)<1\).  Thus \(G'\) satisfies \(\text{ass:hurwitz}\) and \(\text{ass:alias-strip}\).

Construct \(X'_0\sim\mathcal N(m_0,T_W)\), set
\[
 X'_k=W^k(X'_0-x')+x'\qquad(k=0,1,2),
\]
and take mutually independent errors \(\varepsilon'_k\sim\mathcal N(0,E')\), independent of \(X'_0\).  This is a member of the deterministic Gaussian model specified by \(\text{ass:linear-flow}\), \(\text{ass:initial-gaussian}\), \(\text{ass:common-measurement-noise}\), \(\text{ass:measurement-independence}\).  The definition of \(x'\) gives the affine intercept identity
\[
 (I_p-W)x'=m_1-Wm_0.
\]
Consequently the first mean step is \(m_1\), and the probe equation gives the second:
\[
 Wm_1+(I_p-W)x'
 =m_1+W(m_1-m_0)
 =m_1+Wd_0
 =m_1+d_1=m_2.
\]
For covariances, the Stein identity and the raw congruence give successively
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_0)+E'&=T_W+E'=C_0,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_1)+E'&=WT_WW^{\mathsf T}+E'=C_0-H_0=C_1,\\
 \operatorname{Cov}(X'_2)+E'&=W(T_W-H_0)W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=T_W-H_0-WH_0W^{\mathsf T}+E'\\
 &=C_0-H_0-H_1=C_2.
 \end{aligned}
\]
All constructed variables are Gaussian, so equality of these means and covariances is equality of the three marginal laws.  Conversely, the covariance and mean recursions of every explanation in this model give \(WH_0W^{\mathsf T}=H_1\) and \(Wd_0=d_1\); stability and the alias strip give the first two filters, and uniqueness of the Stein solution gives \(T_W=\Sigma\) and \(C_0-T_W=E\succ0\).  Thus the strict-filter intersection is exactly the admissible transition fiber for the three laws.

It remains to verify local openness.  The spectral radius is continuous, and at a matrix whose spectrum avoids \(( -\infty,0]\), the finite spectrum has positive distance from that closed set; continuity of the roots of the characteristic polynomial therefore preserves both spectral conditions under a sufficiently small perturbation.  On the stable set,
\[
 \operatorname{vec}(T_W)
 =\bigl(I_{p^2}-W\otimes W\bigr)^{-1}\operatorname{vec}(H_0),
\]
which is continuous in \(W\).  Positive definiteness of \(C_0-T_W\) is open because its least eigenvalue is positive and continuous.  The admissible set is consequently relatively open in the torsor \(\mathcal F_3\), and every local branch through an admissible point has the torsor dimension computed above.

Because \(H_0^{-1/2}\) is invertible, \(d_0\ne0\) is equivalent to \(r=1\), whereas \(d_0=0\) is equivalent to \(r=0\).  In the latter case the norm certificate is equivalent to \(d_1=0\), because \(H_1^{-1/2}\) is invertible.  Hence the local dimension is \((p-1)(p-2)/2>0\) for \(d_0\ne0\) and \(p\ge3\), and it is \(p(p-1)/2>0\) for \(d_0=0\) and \(p\ge2\).  Moreover, stability implies \(I_p-V\) is invertible and the model mean formula gives
\[
 d_0=(V-I_p)(\mu_0-x^\star).
\]
Thus \(d_0=0\) is exactly the lower-dimensional equilibrium-mean locus \(\mu_0=x^\star\), while \(d_0\ne0\) is generic in the mean parameter.  Finally, if a larger unknown-common-noise model contains this deterministic Gaussian class, every pair or continuum of explanations constructed above remains a pair or continuum in the larger class and has the same three observed laws.  Identification in the larger class would imply identification in every subclass, so the displayed subclass witnesses prove the asserted converse transfer.
body.justification: This theorem gives the exact observable three-snapshot compatibility certificate and the full O(p-r) ambiguity geometry, including the zero-displacement p=2 elbow that generic-only statements miss.
body.gap: Supplied-covariance and known-noise three-time-point results do not characterize the unknown-common-measurement-noise norm certificate, its O(p-r) torsor, or the d_0=0 continuous-ambiguity elbow.
body.consumer: It supplies the sharp three-snapshot nonidentification half of the three-versus-four frontier and transfers that failure to any larger unknown-common-noise model containing this deterministic Gaussian subclass.
